authoring: Direct conversational authorship after primary-paper retrieval; no external LLM API.

evidence.read: Original calculation, pages 2-3, equation 3 and electron/positron comparison.
evidence.finding: A small higher-partial-wave contribution and s-wave phase zero produce a low-energy total-cross-section minimum. The beryllium predictions are theoretical, not measured values.

supplement.finding: Golden and Bandel measured absolute electron-argon cross sections and analyzed their minimum with partial-wave effective-range theory. Only the opened abstract was read; fulltext retrieval failed.

evidence.boundary: No narrow discrete resonance or closed-channel molecular state is required. Gas/particle variants are one pathway; generic interference remains a parent, not a duplicate card for the same experimental setup.

evidence.read: Original experiment and theory, Introduction pages 1-2, equation 1 and shape boundary conditions; experimental phase-boundary discussion.
evidence.finding: The orbital magnetization depends on total induction. Its sufficiently steep differential response destabilizes a uniform state; demagnetizing geometry determines jumps or domain coexistence. Silver phase boundaries were measured using nonlinear pickup response.
evidence.limits: Neither spin exchange nor pinned-wall motion is the origin. Does not assert domains in every sample shape or every quantum-oscillating metal. Material-specific field and temperature values were omitted.

evidence.read: Original numerical/analytical study, classical model and Section III.A equation 26; extensions discussed on page 2.
evidence.finding: Gas impact ionization and ion-driven cathode secondary emission form the self-sustaining loop; the Townsend threshold balances regenerated electrons against losses. Space charge affects the subsequent glow transition.
evidence.limits: One-dimensional local drift model; diffusion, attachment, nonlocal ionization and field-dependent emission are extensions. Self-sustaining does not mean no electrical power.

excluded.read: Acrivos and Herbolzheimer original 1979 paper, pages 455-456.
excluded.reason: The paper explicitly attributes settling-rate enhancement to increased particle-free-fluid production/collection area, not the bulk convective circulation. The proposed card would mainly subdivide existing gravity settling by vessel geometry, so it is excluded.
Existing driven-electron-nuclear-polarization-transfer already covers the proposed pathway.
No accepted boundary beyond avoided-crossing tunneling already covered by landau-zener-avoided-crossing-transfer.
